info.title: Sphericon StaffMember API
info.description: The core API of the Staff console, served on every Instance (ADR 0063): sign-in with a password and a TOTP, the signed-in Staff member, and the Instance's own settings: its Sign-up items with their Legal documents (ADR 0062) and its Telemetry report (ADR 0032). The Enterprise sections are a contract of their own (staffee), served under the same prefix with the same session cookie.

post.description:
Check the password. Answers a challenge (or, at first login, a TOTP enrolment)
and never a session. Unknown email and wrong password answer the same 401.

429.description: RFC 7807 too many requests response: a rate limit was exceeded (ADR 0025)

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The request budget of the window that was exceeded

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix time at which the window resets

post.description:
End the session: bumps the Staff member's session epoch, so every session token of
the Staff member (a copied one too) stops verifying, and clears the session cookie.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description:
The second login step: verify the challenge and a TOTP code, then start the
session (the cookie is set here). At first login the code also confirms the
enrolment. An expired, reused or forged challenge and a wrong code answer the
same 401.

429.description: RFC 7807 too many requests response: a rate limit was exceeded (ADR 0025)

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The request budget of the window that was exceeded

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix time at which the window resets

get.description: The Instance's own settings and state

post.description:
Acknowledge the one-time Telemetry report notice: the first report waits for it. The first
acknowledgement stands, and a repeat changes nothing.

put.description: Switch the Telemetry report on or off. Answers 409 while the environment decides.

get.description:
The Telemetry report exactly as the Instance would send it now (ADR 0032): the body the
published schema describes, built by the code that sends it. Works whether or not sending is
on.
The Instance's Sign-up items, archived ones included, in the order of the sign-up form

post.description:
Add a Sign-up item. A taken key, a mailings consent on an item that is not an optional
consent, and a second mailings consent are refused (422).

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

put.description:
Put the Sign-up items in a new order, the order the sign-up form asks them in. A list that
is not every item's id exactly once is refused (422).

patch.description:
Change a Sign-up item. A blank title, a mailings consent on an item that is not an optional
consent or is archived, and a second mailings consent are refused (422).

post.description:
Archive the Sign-up item: it leaves the sign-up form and its public page at once, and its
published versions stay. Archiving an archived item changes nothing, and an archived item is never
restored. The item that stands for consent to the operator's mailings is refused (422) until
it is unmarked.

put.description:
Save the draft of the item's Legal document. It is edited freely and changes nothing a
visitor sees until it is published.

get.description:
Every published version of the item's Legal document with who published it and when, the
latest first

post.description:
Publish the draft as a new version under a label: it takes effect at once, and is never
changed or removed afterwards. A label the item already has, and an item without a draft,
are refused (422).

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

EntityId.description:
A primary key, written as a decimal string so JavaScript never rounds it. The format
makes the Go servers parse it into an int64: a malformed id is refused as a 400 before
a handler runs. The pattern says the same in the contract, so a client (or a fuzzer) can
tell a malformed id from a valid one without trying it. Eighteen digits is the most a key
reaches, so every id the schema admits fits an int64.

GoneProblem.description: RFC 7807 gone response: the resource existed but is no longer available (an expired link)

InUseProblem.description:
RFC 7807 conflict response for a removal refused because live work still uses the row
(ADR 0049): 409 with `usedBy` naming the users. Every refused removal of a Segment, Tag,
Integration, Sending domain or Automation answers it.

code.description: Why the request was refused, when the client should act on it

type.description: A URI reference that identifies the problem type

title.description: A short, human-readable summary of the problem type

detail.description: A human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence

instance.description: A URI reference that identifies the specific occurrence

retryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying; set on a 429 so a client that only sees the body can show the wait

debug.description: Why a 500 happened, sent only by a development server (`SPHERICON_ENV=development`)

usedBy.description: The live rows that use the one a removal was refused for, never empty

InUseProblemDetails.description: The body of a refused removal (ADR 0049): ProblemDetails plus the rows that use it

LegalDocumentLabel.description: The label a Staff member gives a published Legal document version, unique per item

LegalDocumentMarkdown.description: A Legal document's text, in Markdown

PaymentRequiredProblem.description: RFC 7807 payment required response: the feature needs an Enterprise license

PreconditionRequiredProblem.description:
RFC 7807 precondition required response: the request needs something it did not carry
(a verification link opened outside its Sign-up browser needs a password, ADR 0030)

ProblemCode.description: A machine-readable reason a client branches on, beyond the HTTP status

error.description: The error that failed the request, or the panic value

stack.description: The goroutine stack of a panic; absent for an error a handler returned

requestId.description: The request id the server log carries for this request

method.description: The HTTP method of the failed request

path.description: The path of the failed request

ProblemDebug.description:
What a development server adds to a 500 so the page can show the fault; a production
Instance never sends it

code.description: Why the request was refused, when the client should act on it

type.description: A URI reference that identifies the problem type

title.description: A short, human-readable summary of the problem type

detail.description: A human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence

instance.description: A URI reference that identifies the specific occurrence

retryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying; set on a 429 so a client that only sees the body can show the wait

debug.description: Why a 500 happened, sent only by a development server (`SPHERICON_ENV=development`)

SignupItemKey.description: A Sign-up item's key: its address, and the last segment of its Legal document's public page

SignupItemKind.description: What a Sign-up item asks of a person (ADR 0062)

SignupItemTitle.description: A Sign-up item's title: what the sign-up form shows

qrCode.description: PNG data URI of the URI

StaffEnrolment.description: A TOTP secret awaiting its first confirming code

noticeAcknowledged.description:
Whether a Staff member acknowledged the one-time notice about the Telemetry report. No report
is sent before.

latestRelease.description:
The newest stable release (a bare version such as `0.4.0`) when the Release check found
one newer than the running version; absent otherwise, and always absent for a build whose
version is not a release or in the saas Mode, which makes no Release check.

licenseExpiredAt.description:
When the Instance's license key expired, set only while it has lapsed: the Instance then
runs the open-source core, and nothing Enterprise is deleted (ADR 0035).

telemetrySchemaUrl.description: The page that documents the schema of the Telemetry report

StaffInstanceState.description:
The Instance's own settings and state, which belong to no Workspace (ADR 0063): what a Staff
member sees and decides about the Instance itself.

enabled.description: Whether the Instance sends the Telemetry report

locked.description: Whether the environment decides, which makes the switch in the console read-only

StaffInstanceTelemetry.description: The Telemetry report setting as it applies right now (ADR 0032)

StaffInstanceTelemetryInput.description: Switch the Telemetry report on or off

StaffInstanceTelemetryLock.description: Why the environment, not the Staff member, decides the Telemetry report

StaffLegalDocumentDraftInput.description: Save the draft of an item's Legal document

StaffLegalDocumentPublishInput.description: Publish the draft as a new version

label.description: The label it was published with

publishedAt.description: When it was published, and took effect

publishedBy.description: The Staff member who published it

StaffLegalDocumentVersion.description: A published Legal document version, as the console shows it

StaffLegalDocumentVersionList.description: Every published version of an item's Legal document, the latest (the current one) first

StaffLoginInput.description:
Sign in with an email and password. The email is a plain string: a malformed
address must answer like an unknown one.

StaffLoginOutcome.description:
What the password step granted. There is never a session at this step: a TOTP is
mandatory (ADR 0026). `challenge`: the Staff member has a TOTP, go on with a code.
`enrolment`: the Staff member has none yet (first login); the `enrolment` secret is to be
added to an authenticator app, and the first code confirms it.

challenge.description:
The signed challenge for the second step: bound to the Staff member, valid for 5
minutes, working for one successful second step.

StaffResource.description: The authenticated platform Staff member (shown to customers only as "Sphericon staff")

code.description: A current TOTP code from the authenticator app

StaffSecondFactorInput.description: The second login step: the challenge from the password step and a TOTP code

key.description: Unique across the Instance, and never changed

mailingsConsent.description:
Mark the item as consent to the operator's mailings: only an optional consent, and only
one item of the Instance

StaffSignupItemInput.description: Add a Sign-up item. It goes after the existing ones.

StaffSignupItemList.description: The Instance's Sign-up items, in the order of the sign-up form

StaffSignupItemOrder.description:
The new order of the sign-up form: the id of every Sign-up item, archived ones included, each
once

key.description: The item's key: its Legal document's public page is served under it

position.description: Where the item stands in the sign-up form, smallest first

mailingsConsent.description: Whether the item stands for consent to the operator's mailings

draft.description: The draft of the next version, absent until one is written. A visitor never sees it.

currentVersion.description:
The version in effect, absent until one is published. Visitors see the item only once it
has one.

archivedAt.description:
When the item was archived, absent while it is in use. An archived item is no longer asked
and its public page is gone; its published versions stay.

StaffSignupItemResource.description:
A Sign-up item of the Instance (ADR 0062) with its Legal document's draft and current
version

title.description: A new title. It is not a new version of the Legal document: the form shows it at once.

mailingsConsent.description:
Mark or unmark the item as consent to the operator's mailings: only an optional consent,
and only one item of the Instance

kind.description: What kind of row it is

count.description:
How many rows the entry stands for; absent means one. An `enrollment` entry names the
Automation (id, name) and counts its Enrollments; a `message` entry names it and counts its
sent Outbound messages.

UsedBy.description:
A row that uses the one a removal was refused for: what a client shows to say what to
change first

UsedByKind.description:
What kind of row a refused removal names as a user of the row (ADR 0049). One value per kind
of live user a removal can find, so a client branches on it without parsing text.

WorkspaceId.description:
A Workspace id (ADR 0043): 8 random base62 characters, assigned once at creation and the
Workspace's one public address.
